author: Courant, Richard and Friedrichs, Kurt and Lewy, Hans
title: Über die partiellen Differenzengleichungen der mathematischen Physik
note: Originally published in 1928; the linked source is a later English translation. Background on domains of dependence and the CFL condition.

author: Crank, John and Nicolson, Phyllis
title: A practical method for numerical evaluation of solutions of partial differential equations of the heat-conduction type
journal: Proceedings of the Cambridge Philosophical Society
note: Originally published in 1947; the linked source is a 1996 reprint. This edition implements the theta method for linear diffusion, rather than reproducing the original nonlinear problem.

author: Thomas, Llewellyn Hilleth
title: Elliptic problems in linear difference equations over a network
institution: Watson Scientific Computing Laboratory, Columbia University
note: The original report and a holding URL have not been verified. This provisional record follows the historical citation in Netlib and does not imply direct inspection of the original.

author: Charney, Jule G. and Fjørtoft, Ragnar and von Neumann, John
title: Numerical Integration of the Barotropic Vorticity Equation
note: Publicly accessible original paper. Historical context for stability analysis; the numerical weather forecast is not implemented here.

author: Lax, Peter D.
title: Weak solutions of nonlinear hyperbolic equations and their numerical computation
journal: Communications on Pure and Applied Mathematics
note: Publisher bibliographic record and abstract. Background on weak solutions and Lax-type differences. The Lax shock-tube parameters have not been matched directly to the original table.

author: Lax, Peter D. and Richtmyer, Robert D.
title: Survey of the stability of linear finite difference equations
journal: Communications on Pure and Applied Mathematics
note: Publicly accessible original paper. The equivalence theorem assumes a well-posed linear initial-value problem and a consistent linear approximation.

author: Godunov, Sergei K.
title: A difference method for numerical calculation of discontinuous solutions of the equations of hydrodynamics
note: Original publication in 1959, accepted in 1956. The godunov option in this edition is a Godunov-type finite-volume method with approximate fluxes.

author: Lax, Peter D. and Wendroff, Burton
title: Systems of conservation laws
journal: Communications on Pure and Applied Mathematics
note: Publisher bibliographic record. Background for linear-advection Lax–Wendroff and systems of conservation laws.

author: Fedorenko, Radii P.
title: A relaxation method for solving elliptic difference equations
journal: Zhurnal Vychislitelnoi Matematiki i Matematicheskoi Fiziki
note: Original publication in 1961; English translation in 1962. A historical entry point to multigrid.

author: Rusanov, Vladimir V.
title: The calculation of the interaction of non-stationary shock waves with barriers
journal: Zhurnal Vychislitelnoi Matematiki i Matematicheskoi Fiziki
note: Russian original in 1961; English translation in 1962. This edition uses a modern local Lax–Friedrichs/Rusanov flux.

author: Reed, W. H. and Hill, T. R.
title: Triangular mesh methods for the neutron transport equation
note: Public government-report record. This edition implements modal DG for 1D linear advection, rather than triangular-mesh neutron transport.

author: Hirt, C. W. and Amsden, A. A. and Cook, J. L.
title: An arbitrary Lagrangian-Eulerian computing method for all flow speeds
note: Publisher record and abstract. Historical ALE reference; the implemented example is only a 1D moving-volume uniform-state check.

author: Brandt, Achi
title: Multi-level adaptive solutions to boundary-value problems
note: AMS-hosted original paper. This edition implements a fixed-grid geometric V-cycle, rather than the full adaptive framework.

author: Gingold, R. A. and Monaghan, J. J.
title: Smoothed particle hydrodynamics: theory and application to non-spherical stars
journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
note: Original publisher record. Early SPH paper; this edition implements static 1D kernel reconstruction, not the stellar calculation.

author: Lucy, L. B.
title: A numerical approach to the testing of the fission hypothesis
note: ADS-hosted original article. Independent early particle-method reference; the cubic-spline reconstruction here is not a reproduction of Lucy’s original kernel or dynamics.

author: Gottlieb, David and Orszag, Steven A.
title: Numerical Analysis of Spectral Methods: Theory and Applications
note: Publisher chapter information for a representative spectral-methods monograph. This edition is limited to periodic linear Fourier problems.

author: Sod, Gary A.
title: A survey of several finite difference methods for systems of nonlinear hyperbolic conservation laws
note: The DOI identifies the original paper; the source is an implementation reference for the standard Sod problem and exact solution. The original methods and figures are not reproduced in full.

author: Orszag, Steven A. and Tang, Cha-Mei
title: Small-scale structure of two-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic turbulence
note: The original study concerns incompressible MHD. Distinguish it from the normalization of the modern compressible Orszag–Tang test used here.

author: van Leer, Bram
title: Towards the ultimate conservative difference scheme. V. A second-order sequel to Godunov's method
note: Publisher bibliographic record and abstract. This edition uses selectable-limiter MUSCL with SSPRK3, rather than reproducing the original Lagrangian/remap construction.

author: Hockney, R. W. and Eastwood, J. W.
title: Computer Simulation Using Particles
note: Original book date is 1981, as cited by Barnes and Hut (1986); DOI identifies a later Taylor & Francis reissue. Reference for particle-mesh methods and isolated doubled-domain convolution; the self-cell kernel convention is stated separately in our code.

author: Hockney, R. W.
title: The P³M Code
note: Original newsletter scan hosted by CCP5. Describes mesh forces plus short-range pair corrections. A full P3M solver is not implemented here.

author: Roe, Philip L.
title: Approximate Riemann solvers, parameter vectors, and difference schemes
note: Author-uploaded original full text inspected, including the four Property U conditions on pp.359-360. Independent ideal-gas parameter-vector, eigenbasis, jump and consistency checks accompany single discontinuities and an expansion counterexample. Acoustic entropy smoothing is a separate flux modification.

author: Harten, Amiram and Lax, Peter D. and van Leer, Bram
title: On Upstream Differencing and Godunov-Type Schemes for Hyperbolic Conservation Laws
note: Publicly accessible original paper. Background on HLL; the hll implementation here uses Davis-type minimum/maximum acoustic wave speeds.

author: Woodward, Paul and Colella, Phillip
title: The numerical simulation of two-dimensional fluid flow with strong shocks
note: Author-uploaded original text, Section VI.b setup and corner treatment checked 6 November 2026. The atlas computes first-order HLL Double Mach Reflection and Mach-3 forward-step baselines, not the original PPM figures. The step omits the paper’s entropy/enthalpy corner reset and has one published grid.

author: Barnes, Josh and Hut, Piet
title: A hierarchical O(N log N) force-calculation algorithm
note: Original publisher record. The educational octree uses a geometric opening criterion and compares monopole/full second-moment forces with an identical softened direct sum.

author: Harten, Amiram and Engquist, Bjorn and Osher, Stanley and Chakravarthy, Sukumar R.
title: Uniformly high order accurate essentially non-oscillatory schemes, III
note: Original publication in 1987, distinct from the 1997 reprint. A standalone ENO implementation is planned; this edition implements WENO5-JS.

author: Greengard, L. and Rokhlin, V.
title: A fast algorithm for particle simulations
note: Original paper hosted by a university course. FMM reading reference; multipole-to-local translations and an FMM solver are not implemented here.

author: Turkel, Eli
title: Preconditioned methods for solving the incompressible and low speed compressible equations
note: Publisher bibliographic record and abstract. Low-speed PDE preconditioning is discussed as future work and is distinct from the Jacobi matrix-scaling example.

author: Einfeldt, Bernd
title: On Godunov-Type Methods for Gas Dynamics
note: Publisher bibliographic record and abstract. Background for Einfeldt-type wave-speed estimates in Euler HLLE.

author: Evans, Charles R. and Hawley, John F.
title: Simulation of magnetohydrodynamic flows: A constrained transport method
note: Publicly accessible original paper. This edition uses a Cartesian flux-CT-type construction and does not reproduce every part of the original method.

author: Shu, Chi-Wang and Osher, Stanley
title: Efficient implementation of essentially non-oscillatory shock-capturing schemes
note: Publisher bibliographic record and abstract. Background on TVD Runge–Kutta and flux-based constructions.

author: Cockburn, Bernardo and Shu, Chi-Wang
title: TVB Runge-Kutta local projection discontinuous Galerkin finite element method for conservation laws. II. General framework
note: Original RKDG/TVB paper. Publisher full-text retrieval was unavailable; later author notes: https://www-users.cse.umn.edu/~cockburn/lecture_notes/DG-4.pdf . The atlas has smooth-advection DG and a separate scalar modified-minmod building block, not the complete RKDG/TVB theorem. Duplicate catalog key cockburn1989tvb was merged for unique-source counting.

author: Shu, Chi-Wang and Osher, Stanley
title: Efficient implementation of essentially non-oscillatory shock-capturing schemes, II
note: The DOI identifies the original paper. Initial-condition parameters follow the later Quokka paper. Digitized comparisons with original figures have not been performed.

author: Yoshida, Haruo
title: Construction of higher order symplectic integrators
note: Original paper hosted by a university course. This edition implements the fourth-order triple composition of symmetric Verlet steps on two smooth 1-DOF Hamiltonians.

author: Einfeldt, Bernd and Munz, Claus-Dieter and Roe, Philip L. and Sjögreen, Björn
title: On Godunov-type methods near low densities
note: Publisher bibliographic record and abstract. Background on low-density positivity; this edition uses the standard Toro formulation of the 1–2–3 problem.

author: Jameson, Antony
title: Time dependent calculations using multigrid, with applications to unsteady flows past airfoils and wings
note: The DOI identifies the original paper; the linked source is a later exposition by a coauthor. Dual time stepping here is a minimal linear-advection model.

author: Toro, E. F. and Spruce, M. and Speares, W.
title: Restoration of the contact surface in the HLL-Riemann solver
note: Publisher bibliographic record and abstract. This edition uses HLLC with Davis-type wave speeds and does not implement every original wave-speed estimate or WAF construction.

author: Quirk, James J.
title: A contribution to the great Riemann solver debate
journal: International Journal for Numerical Methods in Fluids
note: Original bibliographic record and abstract; background for shock instability and complementary fluxes. The local stationary planar row-displacement diagnostic is an independent experiment, not a reproduction of the original moving-shock perturbed-grid duct. Blunt-body carbuncle tests remain pending.

author: Barrett, Richard and Berry, Michael and Chan, Tony F. and Demmel, James and Donato, June and Dongarra, Jack and Eijkhout, Victor and Pozo, Roldan and Romine, Charles and van der Vorst, Henk
title: Templates for the Solution of Linear Systems: Building Blocks for Iterative Methods
note: Publicly available author-side reference material for Jacobi, Gauss–Seidel, preconditioning, and multigrid.

author: Liu, Xu-Dong and Osher, Stanley and Chan, Tony
title: Weighted Essentially Non-oscillatory Schemes
note: Publisher bibliographic record and abstract. Historical introduction to WENO; the weights implemented here are Jiang–Shu (1996).

author: Jiang, Guang-Shan and Shu, Chi-Wang
title: Efficient Implementation of Weighted ENO Schemes
note: Publicly accessible original paper. Reference for WENO5-JS flux reconstruction, smoothness indicators, and nonlinear weights.

author: Shewchuk, Jonathan Richard
title: Triangle: Engineering a 2D Quality Mesh Generator and Delaunay Triangulator
booktitle: Applied Computational Geometry: Towards Geometric Engineering
note: Author-hosted paper. Mesh-generation reading reference; the example meshes use Matplotlib triangulation and do not invoke Triangle.

author: Tóth, Gábor
title: The ∇·B = 0 Constraint in Shock-Capturing Magnetohydrodynamics Codes
note: Author-hosted original paper. Reference for CT variants and differences between discrete divergence operators.

author: Pandolfi, Maurizio and D’Ambrosio, Domenic
title: Numerical Instabilities in Upwind Methods: Analysis and Cures for the “Carbuncle” Phenomenon
note: Publisher record and abstract. Linearized shock-instability analysis and localized cures; the proposed methods are not implemented in this edition.

author: Dedner, Andreas and Kemm, Friedemann and Kröner, Dietmar and Munz, Claus-Dieter and Schnitzer, Thomas and Wesenberg, Matthias
title: Hyperbolic Divergence Cleaning for the MHD Equations
note: Publicly accessible original paper, published in 2002 despite 2001 appearing in the DOI. This edition uses a simplified GLM model with fixed cleaning speed.

author: LeVeque, Randall J.
title: Finite Volume Methods for Hyperbolic Problems
note: Publisher bibliographic record and abstract. Background for conservation laws and shallow-water implementations.

author: Hairer, Ernst and Lubich, Christian and Wanner, Gerhard
title: Geometric numerical integration illustrated by the Störmer–Verlet method
note: Original article hosted by a university course. Reference for symplecticity, reversibility, modified equations, and conditional long-time energy estimates; no general exact-energy claim is made.

author: Springel, Volker
title: The cosmological simulation code GADGET-2
journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
note: Author preprint and publisher record. Reference for TreePM force splitting; the separate PM and Tree laboratories do not implement the GADGET code or a complete TreePM pipeline.

author: Abgrall, Rémi
title: Residual distribution schemes: Current status and future trends
note: Author-hosted review. The 2006 date identifies the review, rather than the origin of residual distribution. This edition implements only 1D scalar RD.

author: Nishikawa, Hiroaki and Kitamura, Keiichi
title: Very simple, carbuncle-free, boundary-layer-resolving, rotated-hybrid Riemann solvers
note: Publisher bibliographic record and abstract. The 2D rotated solver and carbuncle tests are future work.

author: Koyama, Hiroshi and Ostriker, Eve C.
title: Gas Properties and Implications for Galactic Star Formation in Numerical Models of the Turbulent, Multiphase Interstellar Medium
note: Published in 2009, with a December 2008 preprint. Section 2.3 and Appendix A give the Cartesian disk-potential FFT method. Our independent kernel laboratory distinguishes the sampled DFT from a continuous Fourier coefficient and does not reproduce the ISM simulations.

author: Toro, Eleuterio F.
title: Riemann Solvers and Numerical Methods for Fluid Dynamics: A Practical Introduction
note: Publisher bibliographic record. Background for exact Riemann solutions and the standard double-rarefaction setup.

author: Williams, Paul D.
title: A Proposed Modification to the Robert–Asselin Time Filter
note: Publisher record identifies the time-filter paper. The ODE laboratory uses unfiltered leapfrog with RK4 startup and does not implement this filter.

author: Fitzpatrick, Richard
title: Fluid Equations in Cylindrical Coordinates
note: Author lecture notes, dated January 22, 2016. Reference for cylindrical fluid operators; the atlas declares its bulk-viscosity and orthonormal-component conventions separately.

author: Kuya, Yuichi and Totani, Kosuke and Kawai, Soshi
title: Kinetic energy and entropy preserving schemes for compressible flows by split convective forms
note: DOI identifies the original 2018 paper. The authors’ 2022 conference explanation, Eq. (9), is the accessible implementation source for our second-order arithmetic-mean Cartesian baseline. Entropy is not claimed exact to roundoff; no shock stabilization is implemented.

author: Shima, Nao and Kuya, Yuichi and Tamaki, Yoshiharu and Kawai, Soshi
title: Preventing spurious pressure oscillations in split convective form discretization for compressible flows
note: Author-university publication record; published in 2021 despite 2020 in the DOI. Pressure-equilibrium-preserving variants are discussed but are not the original arithmetic-mean flux used here.

author: Kuya, Yuichi and Kawai, Soshi
title: Stable and non-dissipative kinetic-energy and entropy preserving (KEEP) schemes for compressible flows
booktitle: Eleventh International Conference on Computational Fluid Dynamics
note: Official conference paper, inspected in full. Section 2.2 Eq. (9) specifies the implemented original Cartesian flux; Section 2.1 explicitly limits exact entropy-conservation claims. Other extensions in the paper are not implemented here.

author: Wibking, Benjamin D. and Krumholz, Mark R.
title: quokka: a code for two-moment AMR radiation hydrodynamics on GPUs
journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
note: Section 3.1.5 of the public paper is the reference for the adopted Shu–Osher parameters. The Quokka code itself is not reproduced.

author: Tamaki, Yoshiharu and Kuya, Yuichi and Kawai, Soshi
title: Comprehensive analysis of entropy conservation property of non-dissipative schemes for compressible flows: KEEP scheme redefined
note: Author-university record and abstract. Analyzes entropy-error terms and redefined KEEP variants with adjustable expansion order; these variants are not implemented in the original-flux exhibit.

author: Asada, Hiroyuki and Maruyama, Kanako and Kawai, Soshi
title: Temporal discretization for improving kinetic-energy and entropy preservation properties in KEEP schemes
note: Publisher record and abstract. Published in 2024 despite 2023 in the DOI. The auxiliary-variable temporal method is not implemented; the exhibit uses classical RK4 with a time-refinement diagnostic.

author: Powell, Ken
title: Philip Lawrence Roe, Professor Emeritus of Aerospace Engineering at the University of Michigan, passed away April 26, 2026, at the age of 87
note: Official university memorial published April 29, 2026. A biographical source, not a numerical-method research paper.

author: Sweby, P. K.
title: High Resolution Schemes Using Flux Limiters for Hyperbolic Conservation Laws
note: Publisher record and abstract inspected. Historical scalar TVD flux-limiter framework, including the compressive limiter due to Roe. The notebook uses explicitly documented slope conventions and a separate MUSCL/SSPRK3 operator.

author: van Leer, Bram
title: Towards the ultimate conservative difference scheme. II. Monotonicity and conservation combined in a second-order scheme
note: Publisher bibliographic record inspected. Historical monotonicity and conservative second-order reconstruction; not a claim to reproduce the original algorithm.

author: Zhang, Xiangxiong and Shu, Chi-Wang
title: On positivity-preserving high order discontinuous Galerkin schemes for compressible Euler equations on rectangular meshes
note: Author-hosted manuscript inspected. Convex admissible Euler states, mean-preserving limiting, and additional flux, quadrature, CFL, and SSP requirements. The atlas implements only a common-state reconstruction scaling building block, not the full time-update scheme.

author: Clawpack Development Team
title: Pyclaw Limiters
note: Official implementation documentation inspected in November 2026; this is an access-year record, not an invention date. Used to distinguish common limiter functions and wave-limiting conventions from the atlas slope reconstruction.

author: MPI-AMRVAC Team
title: Slope Limiters
note: Official code documentation inspected in November 2026; access year only. Implementation notes on minmod, Superbee, MC, van Leer, van Albada variants, and regularization. The atlas uses an explicitly clipped van Albada form without epsilon smoothing.

author: Gottlieb, Sigal and Shu, Chi-Wang and Tadmor, Eitan
title: Strong Stability-Preserving High-Order Time Discretization Methods
note: Author-hosted original manuscript inspected. Conditional inheritance of forward-Euler convex stability, and the distinction between linear and nonlinear SSP. The atlas verifies full-tableau inequalities for its explicit RK methods.

author: Spiteri, Raymond J. and Ruuth, Steven J.
title: A New Class of Optimal High-Order Strong-Stability-Preserving Time Discretization Methods
note: Publisher record and abstract inspected. SSP methods with more stages than their order. The implemented five-stage fourth-order coefficients are taken from the later author-hosted Gottlieb–Ketcheson–Shu review, rather than asserting direct full-text reproduction of this paper.

author: Gottlieb, Sigal and Ketcheson, David I. and Shu, Chi-Wang
title: High Order Strong Stability Preserving Time Discretizations
note: Author-hosted 2008 draft of the 2009 review inspected. Section 3.1 supplies the SSPRK(5,4) decimal coefficients; the atlas converts its state combinations to increments and uses the conservative rounded bound C=1.508. SSP order barriers, low-storage, and alternative families are reading context.

author: Ketcheson, David I.
title: Numipedia: Runge–Kutta method records
note: Author-maintained coefficient and stability records inspected in November 2026; access year, not an invention date. RK44, SSPRK22, and SSPRK43 records cross-check tableaus, scalar polynomials, and absolute-monotonicity radii.

author: Takewaki, H. and Nishiguchi, A. and Yabe, T.
title: Cubic interpolated pseudo-particle method (CIP) for solving hyperbolic-type equations
note: Publisher bibliographic record and indexed abstract inspected; full-text retrieval was unavailable. Early cubic reconstruction with independently specified gradients. The atlas implements a documented constant-speed 1D Hermite case, not all original algorithm variants.

author: Yabe, T. and Aoki, T.
title: A universal solver for hyperbolic equations by cubic-polynomial interpolation I. One-dimensional solver
note: Publisher indexed abstract and bibliographic data inspected; full-text retrieval was unavailable. Value-and-gradient cubic CIP evolution is demonstrated for uniform periodic constant-speed scalar advection only.

author: Yabe, T. and Tanaka, R. and Nakamura, T. and Xiao, F.
title: An Exactly Conservative Semi-Lagrangian Scheme (CIP–CSL) in One Dimension
note: Publisher indexed abstract and bibliographic data inspected; full-page retrieval was unavailable. Integral constraints and exactly conservative CIP-CSL are reading context, not implemented by the basic cubic-CIP example.

author: Saito, Fuyuki and Obase, Takashi and Abe-Ouchi, Ayako
title: Implementation of the RCIP scheme and its performance for 1-D age computations in ice-sheet models
note: Open primary paper inspected. CIP-family value/gradient transport, velocity-gradient terms, and rational reconstruction conventions. The atlas does not implement this RCIP ice-age model or its variable-velocity departure correction.

author: Inutsuka, Shu-ichiro
title: Godunov-type SPH
note: Provisional historical record from reference 9 of Inutsuka (2002). The 1994 original has not been inspected; the source link is the later paper, not a reproduction of the 1994 contribution.

author: Inutsuka, Shu-ichiro
title: Reformulation of Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics with Riemann Solver
note: Author preprint and HTML sections 2–4 inspected for convolution, Gaussian overlaps, pair Riemann states, variable smoothing lengths, matched conservative time updates, and the first shock-tube setup. Reading notes and implementation plan only; the atlas implements kernel interpolation, not GSPH dynamics.

author: Iwasaki, Kazunari and Inutsuka, Shu-ichiro
title: Smoothed particle magnetohydrodynamics with a Riemann solver and the method of characteristics
journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
note: Author preprint inspected for the split between compressive Riemann interactions and Alfvén characteristics, and its test suite. Newtonian particle MHD; separate from relativistic fluid dynamics and the existing grid CT/GLM code. Not implemented here.

author: Kitajima, Kanta and Inutsuka, Shu-ichiro and Seno, Izumi
title: Special relativistic smoothed particle hydrodynamics based on Riemann solver
note: Publisher record and author abstract checked 6 November 2026. Journal issue 15 January 2026; preprint October 2025. SRGSPH addresses unequal baryon numbers, variable smoothing lengths, and relativistic shocks/Kelvin–Helmholtz tests. Special relativity only; no SRGSPH implementation or figure reproduction in this atlas.

author: Wilson, James R.
title: Numerical Study of Fluid Flow in a Kerr Space
note: Original paper inspected for the early Kerr-background gas-flow calculation. Historical reading; not an evolving Einstein–matter solver and not reproduced here.

author: Martí, José M. and Müller, Ewald
title: The analytical solution of the Riemann problem in relativistic hydrodynamics
note: Publisher abstract and bibliographic record inspected. Normal-flow SR Riemann reference; arbitrary transverse velocities need a later extension. Proposed verification source, not an implemented relativistic Riemann solver.

author: Banyuls, F. and Font, J. A. and Ibáñez, J. M. and Martí, J. M. and Miralles, J. A.
title: Numerical 3+1 General Relativistic Hydrodynamics: A Local Characteristic Approach
note: Author-institution bibliographic record checked; formulation context cross-checked against Font (2008). Central Valencia reference, without claiming direct inspection of the complete original or an implemented GRHD solver.

author: Pons, J. A. and Font, J. A. and Ibáñez, J. M. and Martí, J. M. and Miralles, J. A.
title: General Relativistic Hydrodynamics with Special Relativistic Riemann Solvers
note: Author abstract and original-paper scan inspected for the local Minkowskian-coordinate approach connecting GRHD to SR Riemann solvers. Geometric flux/source treatment remains necessary; no solver implemented here.

author: Komissarov, S. S.
title: A Godunov-type scheme for relativistic magnetohydrodynamics
journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
note: Original publisher abstract inspected for multidimensional Godunov-type relativistic MHD and magnetic-flux conservation. Historical reading, not an implemented RMHD method.

author: Gammie, Charles F. and McKinney, Jonathan C. and Tóth, Gábor
title: HARM: A Numerical Scheme for General Relativistic Magnetohydrodynamics
note: Author abstract and publication metadata inspected. Conservative GRMHD, HLL, Tóth-type CT, and a magnetized black-hole torus; original formulation distinguished from later evolving-spacetime frameworks. Not reproduced here.

author: Duez, Matthew D. and Liu, Yuk Tung and Shapiro, Stuart L. and Stephens, Branson C.
title: Relativistic Magnetohydrodynamics in Dynamical Spacetimes: Numerical Methods and Tests
note: Author abstract and journal metadata inspected. Coupled Einstein–Maxwell–MHD with BSSN and conservative matter evolution; historical source for the dynamical-spacetime step. No such coupling implemented here.

author: Noble, Scott C. and Gammie, Charles F. and McKinney, Jonathan C. and Del Zanna, Luca
title: Primitive Variable Solvers for Conservative General Relativistic Magnetohydrodynamics
note: Author abstract and journal metadata inspected for nonlinear conserved-to-primitive recovery and reduced systems. Reading context; current Newtonian primitive conversion is not this relativistic inversion.

author: Font, José A.
title: Numerical Hydrodynamics and Magnetohydrodynamics in General Relativity
note: Open author review inspected for formulations and historical context. Explicitly the 2008 revision, following the 2000 and 2003 versions; used as review context rather than an invention date or a current code-performance comparison.

author: Sądowski, Aleksander and Narayan, Ramesh and Tchekhovskoy, Alexander and Zhu, Yucong
title: Semi-implicit scheme for treating radiation under M1 closure in general relativistic conservative fluid dynamics codes
journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
note: Author abstract and public original inspected for covariant M1 radiation moments and semi-implicit matter interactions in KORAL. Published 2013, preprint 2012. Radiation closure/source integration is reading context, not implemented here.

author: Deppe, Nils and Hébert, François and Kidder, Lawrence E. and Teukolsky, Saul A.
title: A high-order shock capturing discontinuous Galerkin-finite-difference hybrid method for GRMHD
note: Author abstract and publication link inspected. Preprint 2021, journal publication 2022, arXiv update 2024. DG candidate updates and a posteriori FD fallback; not the scalar DG implementation in this atlas.

author: Foucart, Francois
title: Neutrino transport in general relativistic neutron star merger simulations
note: Open author review inspected for leakage, moment, and Monte Carlo transport, including unresolved physical-interaction limits. Review context; no neutrino solver implemented.

author: Deppe, Nils and Foucart, Francois and Bonilla, Marceline S. and others
title: Binary neutron star mergers using a discontinuous Galerkin-finite difference hybrid method
note: Author abstract inspected. Cited as the June 2024 preprint, updated September 2024; a separate journal record was not verified in this review. Demonstration of DG–FD with dynamical-spacetime mergers, not a simulation reproduced here.

author: Fields, Jacob and Zhu, Hengrui and Radice, David and Stone, James M. and Cook, William and Bernuzzi, Sebastiano and Daszuta, Boris
title: Performance-Portable Binary Neutron Star Mergers with AthenaK
note: Author abstract and journal reference checked November 2026. Preprint 2024, journal 2025. Dynamical-spacetime GRMHD, CT, first-order flux correction, and GPU BNS demonstrations; no cross-code speed ranking or local rerun claimed.

author: Kalinani, Jay V. and Ji, Liwei and Ennoggi, Lorenzo and others
title: AsterX: a new open-source GPU-accelerated GRMHD code for dynamical spacetimes
note: Author paper and institution metadata inspected. Online December 2024, 2025 journal issue. GPU-oriented Valencia/Z4c framework with CarpetX/AMReX; source infrastructure does not authorize adding AMR to the atlas, which remains deferred.

author: Cao, Huihui and Peng, Manting and Wu, Kailiang
title: Robust discontinuous Galerkin methods maintaining physical constraints for general relativistic hydrodynamics
note: Publisher abstract, highlights, and record inspected. PCP/OEDG GRHD and primitive recovery under specified formulation/scheme assumptions. Full theorem hypotheses and proofs have not been audited here; no universal positivity or merger-code claim.

author: Musolino, Carlo and Ecker, Christian and Topolski, Konrad and Cassing, Marie and Miler, Keneth and Ng, Harry Ho-Yin and Pierre, Khalil and Most, Elias R. and Rezzolla, Luciano
title: Open-source framework for GPU-accelerated numerical relativity
note: APS accepted-paper page checked 6 November 2026: accepted 2 November 2026, not a verified final volume/page record. July 2026 preprint arXiv:2607.09854 uses the GRACE title prefix. Kokkos, CT, Z4c and merger examples are reported; no local implementation or rerun.

author: Israel, W. and Stewart, J. M.
title: Transient relativistic thermodynamics and kinetic theory
note: Publisher bibliographic record inspected for the transient dissipative-fluid branch. Reading context only; full kinetic derivation and coefficient restrictions have not been audited or implemented.

author: Bemfica, Fábio S. and Disconzi, Marcelo M. and Noronha, Jorge
title: Nonlinear causality of general first-order relativistic viscous hydrodynamics
note: Original author abstract and publisher record inspected. A first-gradient constitutive theory with nonlinear-causality conditions, distinguished from extended-variable theories. Not a universal EOS/transport or discrete-stability guarantee; no viscous relativistic solver implemented.

author: Kovtun, Pavel
title: First-order relativistic hydrodynamics is stable
note: Author abstract and publisher record inspected for stable first-order hydrodynamic frames. Stability results retain the paper assumptions; numerical scheme stability is a separate question. Reading context, not an implemented solver.

author: Courant, Richard
title: Variational methods for the solution of problems of equilibrium and vibrations
journal: Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society
note: Original variational reference. The atlas implements an independent continuous P1 Poisson example; it does not reproduce the original numerical examples.

author: Burgers, Johannes M.
title: A mathematical model illustrating the theory of turbulence
note: Publisher metadata and summary checked. Classical model reference; the gallery implements the inviscid scalar Riemann problem, not viscous Burgers turbulence or original-paper figures.

author: Bhatnagar, P. L. and Gross, E. P. and Krook, M.
title: A Model for Collision Processes in Gases. I. Small Amplitude Processes in Charged and Neutral One-Component Systems
note: Original publisher record checked. Continuous kinetic relaxation source, distinguished from later lattice BGK and its discrete-time viscosity correction. No full-paper numerical reproduction.

author: Lighthill, M. J. and Whitham, G. B.
title: On kinematic waves. II. A theory of traffic flow on long crowded roads
journal: Proceedings of the Royal Society of London. Series A
note: Original bibliographic record and publisher-supplied abstract checked. LWR traffic source; the atlas independently chooses a normalized quadratic fundamental diagram. Full original text was not audited.

author: Richards, Paul I.
title: Shock Waves on the Highway
note: Original publisher record checked. Independent classical traffic-wave source; the atlas uses exact entropy Riemann solutions for its chosen quadratic flux.

author: Chorin, Alexandre Joel
title: Numerical solution of the Navier-Stokes equations
note: Original publisher record and author-hosted original checked. Projection source; the independent periodic MAC/SSPRK2 demonstration is not the original boundary/time algorithm.

author: Alexander, Roger K.
title: Diagonally Implicit Runge-Kutta Methods for Stiff O.D.E.'s
note: Original publisher record checked. Source for the two-stage second-order L-stable SDIRK family; adaptive step doubling in the atlas is a separate implementation choice.

author: Saad, Youcef and Schultz, Martin H.
title: GMRES: A generalized minimal residual algorithm for solving nonsymmetric linear systems
journal: SIAM Journal on Scientific and Statistical Computing
note: Original publisher metadata and abstract checked. Restarted GMRES source; the atlas uses fixed right preconditioning, reorthogonalization, and explicitly recomputed true residuals.

author: van der Vorst, Henk A.
title: Bi-CGSTAB: A Fast and Smoothly Converging Variant of Bi-CG for the Solution of Nonsymmetric Linear Systems
journal: SIAM Journal on Scientific and Statistical Computing
note: Original publisher record checked. BiCGSTAB source; the educational implementation reports true residuals, breakdown and iteration-limit failures. Residual monotonicity is not promised.

author: Qian, Y. H. and d'Humières, D. and Lallemand, P.
title: Lattice BGK Models for Navier-Stokes Equation
note: Original publisher metadata and abstract checked. Lattice BGK source. The D2Q9 model is independently checked using shear-mode decay and a low-Mach channel; no arbitrary-Mach accuracy or full-text reproduction is claimed.

author: Ascher, Uri M. and Ruuth, Steven J. and Spiteri, Raymond J.
title: Implicit-explicit Runge-Kutta methods for time-dependent partial differential equations
note: IMEX RK reading reference; bibliographic metadata checked, full original text not audited. The implemented IMEX Euler is first order and is not attributed to this higher-order RK construction.

author: Guo, Zhaoli and Zheng, Chuguang and Shi, Baochang
title: Discrete lattice effects on the forcing term in the lattice Boltzmann method
note: Original publisher record and abstract checked. Force discretization source; the implementation uses the half-force momentum correction and checks low-Mach Poiseuille profiles against an analytic parabola.

author: Nishikawa, Hiroaki
title: A first-order system approach for diffusion equation. I: Second-order residual-distribution schemes
note: Original publisher metadata and abstract checked, full text not audited. The atlas implements an independent periodic first-order upwind baseline for the equivalent steady system, not the paper's second-order residual-distribution schemes.

author: Nishikawa, Hiroaki
title: A first-order system approach for diffusion equation. II: Unification of advection and diffusion
note: Original publisher metadata and abstract checked. Publication year is 2010 despite 2009 in the DOI. Unified advection-diffusion system is reading/future implementation scope.

author: Chapman, Sydney and Cowling, T. G.
title: The Mathematical Theory of Non-Uniform Gases
note: Original-edition bibliographic preview checked; the 1939 book is not assigned as the invention date of Chapman-Enskog expansion. Third edition appeared in 1970. The atlas gives its own formal unforced isothermal lattice-BGK expansion, not a full audit of this book.

author: Verhulst, Pierre-François
title: Sur la loi d’accroissement de la population (Deuxième mémoire)
journal: Mémoires de l’Académie royale de Belgique
note: Original archival text and metadata available. This is the later 1847 memoir, read in 1846; it must not be labeled the original 1838 logistic note. The early note is not audited in this survey.

author: Michaelis, Leonor and Menten, Maud L.
title: Die Kinetik der Invertinwirkung
note: Original 1913 bibliographic identification through the explicitly labeled Johnson–Goody 2011 translation. This URL identifies the translation, not a 1913 DOI. Original German text not audited; rapid-equilibrium and later quasi-steady-state interpretations are distinguished.

author: Lotka, Alfred J.
title: Analytical Note on Certain Rhythmic Relations in Organic Systems
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
note: Original bibliographic record checked. Early rhythmic organic-system model, before the 1925 book and independent Volterra 1926 source. The survey gives a conventional normalized predator–prey system, not a reproduction of the original figures.

author: Briggs, George E. and Haldane, J. B. S.
title: A Note on the Kinetics of Enzyme Action
note: Original bibliographic record and original-paper search excerpt checked. Quasi-steady-state enzyme-kinetics reference; not conflated with the original rapid-equilibrium interpretation.

author: Volterra, Vito
title: Fluctuations in the Abundance of a Species considered Mathematically
note: Original publisher record and abstract checked. Independent ecological interaction source; Lotka’s earlier publications are cited separately.

author: McKendrick, A. G.
title: Applications of Mathematics to Medical Problems
journal: Proceedings of the Edinburgh Mathematical Society
note: Original first-page text checked: read January 1926, received August 1926, in the 1925–26 session volume. Not dated to the much later online digitization. A later von Foerster lineage is not assigned to this author alone.

author: Kermack, W. O. and McKendrick, A. G.
title: A contribution to the mathematical theory of epidemics
journal: Proceedings of the Royal Society of London. Series A
note: Original publication identified separately from the 1991 reprint. The survey uses the closed homogeneous SIR specialization; it does not reproduce the original general infection-age formulation.

author: Fisher, R. A.
title: The wave of advance of advantageous genes
note: Original publisher metadata and original-text excerpt checked. Population-genetic front source. Fisher–KPP is a conventional family name; the independent KPP 1937 original is not audited here.

author: Monod, Jacques
title: The Growth of Bacterial Cultures
note: Original publisher metadata checked and university-hosted original identified. Historical microbial-growth review; the proposed batch/chemostat benchmark specifies its own yield and feed assumptions.

author: Turing, Alan M.
title: The Chemical Basis of Morphogenesis
journal: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London. Series B
note: University-hosted original text inspected for the model setting and instability premise. The survey’s general two-species reaction–diffusion form is a framework, not one uniquely specified Turing kinetic law.

author: Hodgkin, A. L. and Huxley, A. F.
title: A quantitative description of membrane current and its application to conduction and excitation in nerve
note: Original publisher metadata and the existence of its 2019 modern-convention supplement checked. Physiome CellML encoding identified separately. Voltage offsets, current signs and temperature conventions require an explicitly selected version before implementation.

author: FitzHugh, Richard
title: Impulses and Physiological States in Theoretical Models of Nerve Membrane
note: Original bibliographic record and abstract checked. Two-state excitable/oscillatory model; the survey writes a conventional normalized FitzHugh–Nagumo form, not a claim of identical coefficients or signs across variants.

author: Nagumo, Jinichi and Arimoto, Suguru and Yoshizawa, Shuji
title: An Active Pulse Transmission Line Simulating Nerve Axon
note: Bibliographic cross-check only; full original not inspected. Independent electrical pulse-line contribution cited alongside FitzHugh rather than silently assigning both developments to a single paper.

author: Keller, Evelyn F. and Segel, Lee A.
title: Initiation of Slime Mold Aggregation Viewed as an Instability
note: University-hosted original formulation inspected. It includes more biochemical species than the common two-field Keller–Segel reduction used in the survey. No universal critical mass or original-figure reproduction is asserted.

author: Gierer, Alfred and Meinhardt, Hans
title: A theory of biological pattern formation
note: Original publisher metadata and abstract checked. Short-range activation/long-range inhibition source. The survey states a standard simplified activator–inhibitor variant; full original numerics not reproduced.

author: Peskin, Charles S.
title: Flow patterns around heart valves: A numerical method
note: Bibliographic metadata cross-checked. Immersed-boundary fluid–structure source, distinguished from a biological reaction law. Original full text and valve calculations are not audited or reproduced.

author: Mackey, Michael C. and Glass, Leon
title: Oscillation and Chaos in Physiological Control Systems
note: Publisher-supplied abstract and bibliographic metadata identified; original full text not audited. Delay-equation model requires a full history function, not only a scalar initial value.

author: Gillespie, Daniel T.
title: Exact stochastic simulation of coupled chemical reactions
note: University-hosted original inspected for the master-equation/SSA distinction, reaction-channel sampling and well-mixed setting. Exact refers to sampling the specified continuous-time Markov model, not biological completeness or zero Monte Carlo error.

author: Taylor, Peter D. and Jonker, Leo B.
title: Evolutionary stable strategies and game dynamics
note: Original publisher metadata and abstract checked. Continuous evolutionary-game dynamics source. Stability, ESS and a generic game equilibrium are not interchangeable.

author: Schnakenberg, Jürgen
title: Simple chemical reaction systems with limit cycle behaviour
note: Original publisher metadata and abstract checked. Autocatalytic reaction-network source. The spatial PDE benchmark is a reaction–diffusion extension of chemical kinetics, not automatically a calibrated developmental model.

author: Shigesada, Nanako and Kawasaki, Kohkichi and Teramoto, Ei
title: Spatial segregation of interacting species
note: Original publisher metadata and abstract checked. Cross-diffusion/segregation source. The survey writes a homogeneous-environment reduction, omitting the original environmental-potential terms explicitly.

author: Ablowitz, Mark J. and Zeppetella, Anthony
title: Explicit solutions of Fisher’s equation for a special wave speed
note: Original publisher metadata and abstract checked. Special normalized wave speed ±5/sqrt(6), distinct from the minimal Fisher–KPP speed; dimensional scaling is stated in the survey.

author: Gray, Peter and Scott, Stephen K.
title: Autocatalytic reactions in the isothermal, continuous stirred tank reactor: Isolas and other forms of multistability
note: Original publisher metadata and abstract checked. Well-mixed chemical CSTR source, distinguished from Pearson’s later spatial Gray–Scott pattern study and from a direct biological tissue model.

author: Pearson, John E.
title: Complex Patterns in a Simple System
note: Author preprint abstract and linked journal DOI checked. Spatial reaction–diffusion patterns from finite-amplitude perturbations; pattern appearance is not by itself evidence of a linear Turing instability.

author: Aliev, R. R. and Panfilov, A. V.
title: A simple two-variable model of cardiac excitation
note: Physiome-hosted model encoding and bibliographic identification checked; original full paper not audited. A reduced phenomenological cardiac model, not a detailed human ionic-cell model or a complete bidomain model.

author: Gardner, Timothy S. and Cantor, Charles R. and Collins, James J.
title: Construction of a genetic toggle switch in Escherichia coli
note: Original bibliographic record and abstract checked. Synthetic bistable gene-network source. The survey uses a normalized mutual-repression model, not a complete encoding of experimental induction protocols.

author: Elowitz, Michael B. and Leibler, Stanislas
title: A synthetic oscillatory network of transcriptional regulators
note: Original publisher metadata and abstract checked. Repressilator source; mRNA and protein variables are retained separately in the proposed model, without silently replacing them by a three-state reduction.

author: Johnson, Kenneth A. and Goody, Roger S.
title: The Original Michaelis Constant: Translation of the 1913 Michaelis–Menten Paper
note: Translation bibliographic record checked. This is a 2011 translation/commentary route to the 1913 original, not an original publication dated 2011.

author: Murray, J. D.
title: Mathematical Biology I: An Introduction
note: Publisher edition metadata checked: third edition print copyright 2002, later eBook publication distinguished. Broad reading reference, not a substitute for original papers or an audited source of every parameter.

author: Arakawa, Akio and Lamb, Vivian R.
title: Computational Design of the Basic Dynamical Processes of the UCLA General Circulation Model
booktitle: Methods in Computational Physics: Advances in Research and Applications
note: Original chapter and bibliographic identity located; full PDF extraction exceeded tool size limits. A/B/C layout is cross-checked with ECMWF/MITgcm documentation. The atlas independently derives and tests centered periodic f-plane Fourier symbols, not a reproduction of the complete UCLA dynamical core.

author: Riddaway, R. W. and Hortal, M.
title: Numerical methods
institution: ECMWF Meteorological Training Course Lecture Series
note: Official teaching notes inspected for horizontal staggering and A–E grid relationships. PDF carries ECMWF 2002 and revised March 2001, not a new original invention date. Used as an exposition, distinct from Arakawa–Lamb 1977.

author: MITgcm contributors
title: C grid staggering of variables
note: Official living documentation checked on 6 November 2026. Year denotes access, not invention. Face-normal three-dimensional placement reference; no assertion that the atlas uses the full MITgcm algorithm.

author: Dahlquist, Germund G.
title: A special stability problem for linear multistep methods
note: Original publisher metadata and abstract checked. Foundational A-stability reference in the linear-multistep setting; full text not audited. The atlas distinguishes one-step stability functions, multistep root conditions, stiff damping and spatial error norms.

author: NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions
title: Classical orthogonal polynomials: definitions, weights and recurrence relations
note: Living mathematical reference, checked November 2026. Sections 18.2, 18.3 and 18.9 consulted for domains, weights, normalization and recurrences; the year denotes this consultation, not the historical origin of Legendre polynomials.

author: Teukolsky, Saul A.
title: Short note on the mass matrix for Gauss-Lobatto grid points
note: Author preprint posted in December 2014, full HTML consulted. Explains exact and GLL-quadrature mass matrices and their rank-one difference. The reference-element notebook tests this distinction; it is not a reproduction of a full spectral-element PDE solver.

author: Brio, Moysey and Wu, Cheng-chin
title: An upwind differencing scheme for the equations of ideal magnetohydrodynamics
note: Original bibliographic record for the Brio-Wu coplanar shock tube. Publisher metadata checked; no claim of full-text inspection or exact-solution reproduction. The local HLLD/HLLE comparison records its gamma=2 initial states and numerical grid comparison.

author: Miyoshi, Takahiro and Kusano, Kanya
title: A multi-state HLL approximate Riemann solver for ideal magnetohydrodynamics
note: Original HLLD bibliographic record; publisher abstract/metadata, not the complete original paper, inspected. Star and double-star equations cross-checked against the linked official Athena++ implementation. The local independent implementation has contact, rotational-wave and standard-test checks; no Athena++ output is reproduced.

author: Mignone, Andrea and Tzeferacos, Petros
title: A second-order unsplit Godunov scheme for cell-centered MHD: The CTU-GLM scheme
note: Public author manuscript inspected for the conservative GLM equations and longitudinal cleaning subsystem. The local loop test uses MC/SSPRK2 and split psi damping, not the paper's CTU integrator or EGLM variant.

author: Mignone, Andrea and Del Zanna, Luca
title: Systematic construction of upwind constrained transport schemes for MHD
note: Public 2020 author manuscript inspected, especially CT-Contact equations 20-22. The local shared-corner update uses contact-upwinded transverse EMF derivatives and verifies the one-dimensional face-flux limit; UCT-HLLD itself is not implemented.

author: Colella, Phillip and Woodward, Paul R.
title: The Piecewise Parabolic Method (PPM) for gas-dynamical simulations
note: Original 1984 journal metadata; linked public author report is the earlier July 1982 preprint and was inspected for parabolic interpolation/monotonicity. The local method-of-lines limited parabolic FV excludes wave tracing, contact steepening, shock flattening and Lagrange/remap; it is not a full original-PPM reproduction.

author: Borges, Rafael and Carmona, Monique and Costa, Bruno and Don, Wai Sun
title: An improved weighted essentially non-oscillatory scheme for hyperbolic conservation laws
note: Original 2008 publisher metadata/abstract inspected. A public 2006 three-author earlier manuscript was also consulted and has different weight conventions; no complete final-paper inspection is claimed. The local FD WENO-Z variant explicitly defines tau5=abs(beta0-beta2), exponent 2 and epsilon=1e-6, with characteristic/component tests and smooth refinement.

author: Liou, Meng-Sing and Steffen, Christopher J., Jr.
title: A New Flux Splitting Scheme
note: Original AUSM publisher metadata/abstract inspected; no full 1993-paper inspection is claimed. The independent local AUSM-family baseline uses common arithmetic sound speed and cubic pressure splitting, cross-checked with official FEST-3D documentation, and is not every original variant or AUSM+-up.

author: Liou, Meng-Sing
title: A Sequel to AUSM: AUSM+
note: Publisher metadata/abstract inspected. AUSM+ is a separately planned extension; its original wave-speed/pressure choices and properties are not claimed by the local common-sound-speed AUSM baseline.

author: Liou, Meng-Sing
title: A sequel to AUSM, Part II: AUSM+-up for all speeds
note: Publisher metadata/abstract inspected. Planned all-speed AUSM-family extension; the local baseline has no AUSM+-up pressure/velocity correction or low-Mach verification.

author: FEST-3D Team
title: FEST-3D documented AUSM source
note: Official source documentation generated 10 February 2020. Consulted to cross-check common arithmetic interface sound speed, Mach polynomials, cubic pressure fractions and enthalpy transport. The local independent vectorized implementation does not use FEST-3D output.

author: Hirsch, Charles
title: Numerical Computation of Internal and External Flows: The Fundamentals of Computational Fluid Dynamics
note: Publisher edition record and contents checked. Cites the 2007 second-edition fundamentals volume, not the complete original two-volume set. Reading reference for discretization, grid properties, stability and flow solvers; not an audited implementation source for every chapter.

author: LeVeque, Randall J.
title: Finite Difference Methods for Ordinary and Partial Differential Equations: Steady-State and Time-Dependent Problems
note: Author-maintained book list checked for year, title, DOI and companion materials. Reading reference for consistency, stability, boundary-value problems and time stepping; full book not audited here.

author: Patankar, Suhas V.
title: Numerical Heat Transfer and Fluid Flow
note: Current publisher first-edition record and contents checked; copyright year 1980. The linked CRC/Routledge record is a current listing of the work. Reading reference for conservative control-volume discretization and pressure-velocity coupling, not evidence of a complete SIMPLE implementation here.

author: Ferziger, Joel H. and Perić, Milovan and Street, Robert L.
title: Computational Methods for Fluid Dynamics
note: Publisher edition metadata and contents checked. Uses the fourth-edition copyright year 2020; the publisher lists electronic publication in August 2019. Broad CFD reading reference, including incompressible flow and solution procedures; not a validation claim for all listed applications.

author: Saad, Yousef
title: Iterative Methods for Sparse Linear Systems
note: Publisher second-edition record and author-maintained book page checked; original first edition was 1996. Author page provides the text and errata. Reading reference for Krylov methods and preconditioning; original algorithm papers remain separate citations.

author: Golub, Gene H. and Van Loan, Charles F.
title: Matrix Computations
note: Fourth-edition publication and contents checked in the SIAM distribution record; publisher is Johns Hopkins University Press. Reading reference for factorizations, conditioning, eigenproblems and sparse systems; no claim of full-text audit.

author: Trefethen, Lloyd N.
title: Spectral Methods in MATLAB
note: Author-maintained book page checked: SIAM 2000, sample chapters, programs and errata. Reading reference for spectral differentiation and boundary-value problems; the author notes limited treatment of barycentric interpolation.

author: Hesthaven, Jan S. and Warburton, Tim
title: Nodal Discontinuous Galerkin Methods: Algorithms, Analysis, and Applications
note: Publisher copyright-edition record and contents checked: 2008. Reading reference for nodal bases, element operators and DG fluxes. The atlas currently has selected educational DG and basis examples, not all systems treated in the book.

author: Hairer, Ernst and Lubich, Christian and Wanner, Gerhard
title: Geometric Numerical Integration: Structure-Preserving Algorithms for Ordinary Differential Equations
note: Publisher second-edition record and description checked. Reading reference for symplectic and symmetric methods, splitting and long-time behavior; symplecticity is distinct from exact conservation of the original Hamiltonian.

author: Durran, Dale R.
title: Numerical Methods for Fluid Dynamics: With Applications to Geophysics
note: Publisher second-edition copyright record and description checked. Retitled revision of the earlier geophysical wave-equation text. Reading reference for wave propagation, dispersion, advection and time discretization; not a complete spherical dynamical-core implementation.

author: Kageyama, Akira and Sato, Tetsuya
title: The Yin-Yang Grid: An Overset Grid in Spherical Geometry
note: Author preprint inspected for patch bounds, coordinate rotation and vector transformation. Atlas diagrams illustrate geometry only; overlap interpolation and a conservative flow solver are not implemented.

author: Ronchi, C. and Iacono, R. and Paolucci, P. S.
title: The Cubed Sphere: A New Method for the Solution of Partial Differential Equations in Spherical Geometry
note: Publisher bibliographic search record checked; full text not inspected. Atlas uses an explicitly specified equiangular gnomonic diagram and does not reproduce the paper solver.

author: Wan, H. and Giorgetta, M. A. and Zängl, G. and Restelli, M. and Majewski, D. and Bonaventura, L. and Fröhlich, K. and Reinert, D. and Rípodas, P. and Kornblueh, L. and Förstner, J.
title: The ICON-1.2 hydrostatic atmospheric dynamical core on triangular grids – Part 1: Formulation and performance of the baseline version
note: Official model-description record and abstract checked for the triangular-grid C-staggering connection. Atlas midpoint-refined icosahedron and barycentric dual are illustrative, unoptimized meshes, not the ICON grid or dynamical core.

author: Fletcher, Clive A. J.
title: Computational Techniques for Fluid Dynamics 1: Fundamental and General Techniques
note: Publisher second-edition record and contents checked. Year follows the listed April 1991 print publication; the same current record displays copyright 1998 and eBook release 2012, which must not be mistaken for a new algorithm date. Reading reference for the textbook scope, not a claim of full-text audit or reproduction of every algorithm.

author: Fletcher, Clive A. J.
title: Computational Techniques for Fluid Dynamics 2: Specific Techniques for Different Flow Categories
note: Publisher second-edition record and contents checked: print and copyright 1991; eBook release 2012 is a later digital issue. Reading reference for the textbook scope, not a claim of full-text audit or reproduction of every algorithm.

author: Briggs, William L. and Henson, Van Emden and McCormick, Steve F.
title: A Multigrid Tutorial
note: Publisher book record, contents and front-matter metadata checked. Second edition published in 2000; the 2012 online publication date is a later digital issue. Introductory reading on smoothing, coarse-grid correction, implementation, nonlinear problems and AMG. The atlas geometric Poisson V-cycle is a limited educational baseline, not a reproduction of the entire book.

author: Trottenberg, Ulrich and Oosterlee, Cornelius W. and Schüller, Anton
title: Multigrid
note: Publisher first-edition description and contents checked. Uses the conventional 2001 bibliographic year, also cited in Elsevier reference material; the current publisher shop lists release on November 20, 2000. Reference for multigrid theory, local Fourier analysis, parallel methods, systems and AMG. Full text not audited; these topics are not all implemented in the atlas.
